set_aside.subject: new-store creation in WAL mode under a temporary name
set_aside.text: “a store made new is made in SQLite's write-ahead-log mode” together with “under a temporary name and renaming it once complete, after removing a leftover of that name and no other file”
set_aside.question: Who owns the WAL and shared-memory sidecars of the temporary database, and what must happen to them on completion, interruption, restart and rename so that the renamed store contains every committed initialization change while no forbidden extra file is removed?
options: Checkpoint and close the temporary database before renaming its main file, with a specified treatment of any remaining sidecars
Rename the main database and its WAL/SHM sidecars as one installation operation
Avoid creating sidecars under the temporary name while still satisfying the requirement that the new store is made in WAL mode
set_aside.default_guess: Checkpoint and close the temporary database, verify that all initialization is in the main file, then rename only that file.

witness.initial: The configured store is absent and Registry starts creating its replacement under the declared temporary name in WAL mode.
events: store creates the temporary SQLite database and commits its schema and release version while WAL data exists
the process is interrupted, or store renames only the main temporary file before the WAL contents are incorporated
the next start removes only the file of the temporary name and no other file, then opens or recreates the configured store
outcomes: The implementation checkpoints and closes before rename; the configured store contains the complete schema and version and no temporary sidecar affects the next start.

The implementation treats rename of the main file as sufficient; committed initialization remains in a sidecar under the temporary name, or stale temporary sidecars survive and affect or obstruct recreation.
witness.observer: instance_lifecycle, which either starts successfully on the complete store or fails/opens an incomplete store

set_aside.subject: backup snapshot timestamp
set_aside.text: The changed store passage says “the snapshot fixed by its first read, of the audit counter, with the clock read then”, while the unchanged Time passage says “a backup's instant is the one `store` reads when the copy's read transaction begins”
set_aside.question: Is the backup instant read when the read transaction begins or when its first read fixes the snapshot, and if those are separate operations, on which side of the audit-counter read must the clock be sampled?
options: Use the instant read when the transaction begins
Read the clock immediately before the first audit-counter read that fixes the snapshot
Read the clock immediately after that first read succeeds
set_aside.default_guess: Read the clock immediately after the audit-counter read that successfully fixes the snapshot.

witness.initial: A backup read transaction has begun but has not yet read the audit counter; the wall clock can advance or be adjusted and an action transaction can commit before the first read.
events: store begins the backup read transaction
the clock changes and an action commits
store performs the first read of the audit counter, fixing the snapshot
outcomes: Following the unchanged Time passage, the backup records the earlier transaction-begin instant although its snapshot includes the later commit.
Following the changed store and A18 passages, it records the later first-read instant for the snapshot that includes the commit.
witness.observer: the owner reading backup metadata and reasoning about which committed changes the backup contains
